title: Maximum Number of Removable Characters
summary: Given two strings, s and p, where p is a subsequence of s, and an array of distinct indices from s, determine the maximum number of indices you can remove from s using the first k indices in the array, such that p still remains a subsequence of the modified s.
statement: Given two strings, s and p, where p is a subsequence of s, and an array of distinct indices from s, determine the maximum number of indices you can remove from s using the first k indices in the array, such that p still remains a subsequence of the modified s. Specifically, mark the characters at s[removable[i]] for each 0 <= i < k, remove all marked characters, and check if p is still a subsequence of the remaining string. Return the largest k for which p remains a subsequence after the removals.
constraints: 1 <= len(p) <= len(s) <= 100000 and p initially is a subsequence of s.
removable contains distinct valid indices and may be empty.
Remove exactly the first k listed indices and maximize k while p remains a subsequence.
hints: If p survives the first k removals, it survives every smaller prefix, giving a monotonic predicate.
For a candidate k, mark its removed indices and scan s and p with two pointers.
Binary-search the largest k whose scan matches all of p.
Prefix nesting proves monotonicity, the scan exactly tests subsequence order, and upper-mid search retains the largest passing boundary.
editorial: Prefix nesting proves monotonicity, the scan exactly tests subsequence order, and upper-mid search retains the largest passing boundary.

tests.explanation: After removing indices three and one, a and b remain; removing index zero next destroys the subsequence.
Only the first listed removal can occur while retaining a-b-c-d in order.
